finding.claim: A malicious or compromised MCP server can cause the client to send the stored refresh_token and client_id/client_secret to an attacker-chosen token endpoint, via a resource_metadata URL in a 401 WWW-Authenticate header.
finding.source: resource_metadata parameter in the WWW-Authenticate header of a 401 response from the MCP server (attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: http_post_form to token_endpoint in flow.rb:707 with refresh_token in form body and Basic auth header built at flow.rb:693-697.

trace.note: Faraday::UnauthorizedError rescued; run_oauth_flow! invoked when @oauth set.
run_oauth_flow! parses resource_metadata from the 401 challenge.
attempt_refresh calls flow.refresh! with attacker-supplied resource_metadata_url whenever a refresh token is stored.
refresh! reads stored refresh_token.
Only ensure_secure_url! (HTTPS) applied to resource_metadata_url; no same-origin requirement.
locate_authorization_server fetches attacker PRM.
authorization_servers[0] taken from attacker PRM; only HTTPS checked.
canonical_resource only checks PRM resource coverage if PRM sets resource; attacker can omit it.
Stored client_information (including client_secret) reused unconditionally.
exchange_refresh_token builds form containing refresh_token.
Issuer check only verifies self-consistency with attacker-controlled AS metadata.
Form and Basic credentials POSTed to attacker token_endpoint.

finding.guards_checked: HTTPS-only (flow.rb:154, 237, 266); PRM resource coverage via resource_covers? (discovery.rb:306, only when PRM sets resource); issuer equality (flow.rb:262, self-consistency only); OAuthURLGuard (http.rb:354) covers only MCP URL, not token endpoint, and is absent from Flow's own Faraday client; no pinning of the AS that issued the stored tokens. Precondition: malicious/compromised MCP server or a server returning a crafted 401; not reachable by a network MITM because of TLS.

finding.claim: A non-object element in a JSON-RPC batch array crashes the stdio server process, because request[:id] raises TypeError outside the rescue block.
finding.source: Stdin line from the spawning peer containing a batch such as [1] or ["x"].
finding.sink: request[:id] in process_request (json_rpc_handler.rb:72), outside the begin/rescue at json_rpc_handler.rb:104-127.

trace.note: Each stdin line passed to @session.handle_json.
Server#handle_json delegates to JsonRpcHandler.handle_json.
Batch array elements mapped through process_request.
request[:id] on Integer/String raises TypeError; no rescue on this path.
handle_json rescues only JSON::ParserError.
open rescues only RequestHandlerError and Interrupt; TypeError escapes and terminates the server loop.

finding.guards_checked: HTTP transport not affected: streamable_http_transport.rb:457-459 rejects non-Hash bodies before dispatch. Only stdio transport and direct Server#handle_json callers are reachable. Impact is availability only.

finding.claim: A malicious MCP server can make the client issue GET requests to attacker-chosen URLs, including http://127.0.0.1 loopback targets, because metadata URLs are not filtered for private or internal addresses.
finding.source: resource_metadata from the WWW-Authenticate header, and authorization_servers from the attacker-supplied PRM.

trace.note: resource_metadata taken from 401 challenge.
run! validates resource_metadata_url scheme only.
locate_authorization_server fetches PRM.
fetch_protected_resource_metadata builds candidate URLs.
fetch_metadata_json issues GET per candidate URL.
http_get performs the request with no address filtering.

finding.guards_checked: secure_url? (discovery.rb:181-194) requires HTTPS, but permits http for loopback hosts; no private-address or DNS-rebinding filtering; errors swallowed at flow.rb:231-233 and flow.rb:257-259, so the request is effectively blind with only status and timing observable.

finding.claim: Stateful Streamable HTTP sessions have no ownership check unless the application supplies session_request_validator; anyone holding a leaked Mcp-Session-Id can use the session, including DELETE.
finding.source: Mcp-Session-Id header value (random UUID, but exposed to anything that can observe headers, such as proxy logs or plain HTTP).
finding.sink: Session-scoped requests at streamable_http_transport.rb:488-490, GET at :526, DELETE at :549.

trace.note: validate_session_request returns true when no session_request_validator is configured.
Origin-consistency check only applies when both origins are present; not authentication.
Ownership gate applied to all session requests when validator returns true.
DELETE allowed for any caller passing the gate.

finding.guards_checked: Origin-consistency check (streamable_http_transport.rb:626); session_request_validator hook (documented at lines 73-80 as the deployer's responsibility). Documented by design, not a code defect; listed as low severity for deployments that omit the validator.
